Revised assessment using Beige Book insights:
- Policy stance: The FOMC’s March 2019 hold and “patient” guidance are consistent with mixed real-side signals and muted inflation.
- Beige Book corroboration: Labor markets remain tight with widespread worker shortages (IT, manufacturing, trucking, restaurants, construction) and rising wages across both low- and high-skilled positions, alongside enhanced non-wage compensation. However, consumer spending was restrained by harsh winter weather and higher credit costs; manufacturing faced softer global demand, tariffs, and policy uncertainty; and some federal shutdown effects were noted in Jan–Feb.
- Credit channel: Tighter bank standards and softer loan demand (per SLOOS) reinforce headwinds, raising the risk of amplifying financial accelerator dynamics if policy were tightened further.
- Net tone: Despite wage pressures, the broader mosaic—slower household/business spending, credit tightening, and external/manufacturing drags with subdued inflation—tilts dovish and validates a pause.
